status: Accepted requirements on 23 October 2026; not implemented or cut over.
scope: MXF damage boundaries only; approved field contracts and source-opening rules preserved.

proposal.selectedHeaderFoundation: Require trustworthy complete selected-region framing and needed mapping/ownership foundations, not successful decoding of every optional value or whole-file Complete.
proposal.value: Withhold a safely bounded damaged value and dependent calculations; retain independent usable facts under approved field rules.
proposal.objectOrRelationship: Withhold dependent facts when identity or association is unsafe; retain independently qualified branches.
proposal.sharedStructure: Do not publish metadata from an unsafe selected region or arbitrary structural prefix; keep physical row and independent PMR/MDB/filesystem facts.
proposal.unknownOrExternal: Safely bounded unknown optional data and legitimate external references are not automatic corruption; unavailable needed dependency remains unavailable.
proposal.otherOutcomes: Distinguish I/O, cancellation, changing source, unsupported layout and resource failure; no blanket corrupt-file catch.
proposal.unchangedScope: No new priorities, header opens, footer recovery, repair, essence verification, runtime implementation or app cutover.

mediaComposer.scope: Bounded read-only installed Media Composer native MXF damage-handling audit. Fifteen fresh named ARM64 function captures and scanner vtable bytes. No application/private API/GUI execution, damaged-file execution, media read/write, build, test, fuzz run, benchmark or runtime source edits.

findings.topic: Native MXF opening and root restoration can fail at file scope
anchors: MXFDomain::IMXFDomain_InitAAFData 0x470608: cached-storage allocator failure 0x470928..0x47094c, raw-storage creation failure 0x470994..0x4709b8.

Reading open call 0x470a64 tests negative status; generic failure branch 0x470c94..0x470cb4 raises an XError. Separate create/open fallback branches exist for specific statuses; no blanket recovery rule.
Header/dictionary acquisition failure messages occur at 0x470ef8 and 0x470f64.

MXFDomain::New 0x46fa30 catches initialisation errors, tears down and reraises MXFDomain_INIT_FAILED or MXFDomain_IN_USE for file streams at 0x46fdcc..0x46fe08; separate non-file-stream failure 0x46fe2c..0x46fe34.
findings.meaning: An unusable storage/root/header import is not treated as a successful collection of all optional blank values. These are native import failures; no physical-media inventory or GUI-row survival claim follows.

findings.topic: Typed toolkit restoration distinguishes some skippable unknown properties from errors
anchors: OMKLVStoredObject::restore(OMFile&) 0x1b1494 loops metadata keys. Failed next-key read branches 0x1b19e8 to exception construction at 0x1b1b88..0x1b1bb4: Failed to read key while parsing metadata.
Separate no-valid-metadata branch constructs OMException at 0x1b1bbc..0x1b1be8.
OMKLVStoredObject::flatRestore 0x1b388c maps local tag through dictionary at 0x1b3950 and tests isAllowed at 0x1b3a14; false goes to property skipping at 0x1b3910, then next property.
The checked property-set failure path 0x1b3a24..0x1b3a28 can reach OMException Property does not belong to property set at 0x1b3fe8..0x1b4014.

Primer reader 0x1b53c0 obtains recorded batch count/stride at 0x1b5414/0x1b542c and installs local-tag/key mappings at 0x1b54d4. Header-partition reader 0x1bf7a4 obtains typed partition fields and container labels.
findings.meaning: Some unknown but traversable properties are skipped; structural or object-model failures can abort restoration. Finding named checks/readers does not prove complete validation of every malformed Primer, length, reference or property form.

findings.topic: Ownership and essential physical-descriptor failures are not mere display-field misses
anchors: LocalMDB::ScanMXFFileToMobManager 0x41b924 calls MXFDomain::New at 0x41ba48; unsupported operational-pattern branch raises MXFDomain_INIT_FAILED at 0x41ba9c..0x41babc.
Missing mob enumerator error branch 0x41bd88..0x41bda8; invalid stream offset branch 0x41bf7c..0x41bfb0.
The expected physical file-descriptor cast is checked at 0x41bfcc..0x41bfd4; NULL error raised at 0x41bfd8..0x41bff8.
findings.meaning: Native checks important object/physical-descriptor assumptions. These specific import errors do not establish a universal rule for every optional broken link or a Bella permission to substitute another unqualified owner.

anchors: AAFDomain::GetStringPropFromObject 0x4ca0c performs property-definition/presence/value lookup; 0x4caac..0x4cae0 returns a negative status for unproved presence. Typed string extraction failure branches 0x4cb74..0x4cb9c release temporary buffer rather than publish a successful string.
A genuine zero-length typed string yields an allocated empty string at 0x4cb88..0x4cb98, separate from unsuccessful getter status.
AAFDomain::GetMobIDPropFromObject 0x4d7ac calls the record getter using tdMobIDType and an exact 32-byte request at 0x4d7d4..0x4d808.

AFileMediaDesc::GetAAFProperties 0x17c930: negative Length status logs Missing length and clears success at 0x17ca0c..0x17ca24; negative SampleRate similarly at 0x17ca64..0x17ca7c. Function returns the success flag at 0x17cc38.
ImplAAFDigitalImageDescriptor::GetCompression 0xdc20c checks property presence at 0xdc248; absent branch returns negative status, whereas present property extraction can return success.
findings.meaning: Native distinguishes some absent/empty/success/failure cases at typed API boundaries. Required descriptor-field failures can invalidate the descriptor import. This is not one universal preserve-every-other-field rule; callers decide how statuses affect import.

findings.topic: Per-file rejection and scan continuation have explicit boundaries
anchors: Fresh MSMDBMediaStreamMgr vtable +0x2c8 maps to ScanFileToCache 0x44cea0; +0x2d8 maps to ScanMXFFileToCache 0x44e184.

ScanDirectoryToCache calls +0x2c8 at 0x44c7e4..0x44c7fc, then increments progress/entry state at 0x44c800..0x44c838 and loops to the next entry. A normal false return is not checked as a directory abort here.
The MXF reader rejects unsupported operational patterns via 0x44e650..0x44e674 and returns false after cleanup at 0x44e86c.
Per-file MXF exception handlers at 0x44ecf0..0x44ee74 capture/log errors and reach shared cleanup. That cleanup explicitly tests OUT OF MEMORY and reraises it at 0x44e810..0x44e830.
ScanFileToCache also has caught-error cleanup with possible reraising at 0x44d2f0..0x44d2fc. Directory-level caught-error cleanup can reraise at 0x44c89c..0x44c8a8.
findings.meaning: A rejected individual MXF can allow the native directory scan to continue. This is not a guarantee that every exception returns false, every partial result is discarded, or every error is recoverable. Memory/resource and directory-level failures can propagate.

bellaImplicationInference: Keep the already-required physical row even when its MXF metadata cannot be used. Native catalogue insertion success is not the same as Bella physical-file discovery.

Use explicit small boundaries: an unusable scalar with safe surrounding framing does not manufacture a value; an unproved owner/reference cannot supply dependent fields; unsafe selected-header framing stops that header read.

Keep independent established facts only when their own bytes, types, ownership and relevant enclosing boundaries remain usable. Do not salvage by blind searching for byte patterns beyond a lost boundary.

Unknown but safely bounded unneeded properties can be skipped; unsupported format is not automatically corruption. Missing, empty, damaged and conflicting values must retain their already-agreed field meanings.
Do not copy native fallback/default status handling blindly. Already reviewed compression/alpha import can coalesce negative statuses; Bella has separately agreed narrower proof requirements.

Ordinary single-file damage should not cancel unrelated file work. Cancellation, inability to enumerate a location, memory/resource failure and other job failures need explicit scanner outcomes rather than a false claim the whole scan completed.
No new media-header opening trigger, source priority, footer navigation/search or recovered value precedence is authorised by this native review. Root owns the final Bella proposal.
limits: Static branch inspection, not malformed-file execution. No crash resistance, absence of hangs, universal recovery, read-volume limit or runtime performance claim.
The installed toolkit is the MXF-domain dependency identified by prior native work. Every dynamic storage subclass and failure route was not reconstructed.

Primer/header typed-reader existence is not proof that every count, stride, BER length or reference is validated safely. The reviewed BER reader has a width check after a raw read; it is not a defensive parsing implementation to copy.

No claim Media Composer preserves every other field after arbitrary damage, or that every generic per-file catch returns false. Explicit OUT OF MEMORY propagation is established; other partial-import effects are not exhaustively modelled.
No final GUI or directory scan was observed, and no reader was invoked on user media. The native physical-file/cache behaviour is not automatically Bella row-retention policy.

mdvx.scope: Bounded read-only MDVx arm64 ordinary MXF damage-handling/native branch review; fresh binary/disassembly and raw function hashes. No comparison-commit input.
mdvx.method: Fresh installed binary and otool arm64 disassembly, byte-identical to prior audited dump. Extracted 30 complete relevant native functions; retained file/virtual offsets and raw code digests. Independently decoded wrapper return-switch bytes and CFString diagnostics. No damaged input execution or app/private API invocation.
mdvx.mainFinding: Embedded libMXF/ami_read_info propagates many structural/required-value failures and cleans up; it skips recognized-as-unknown sets/items rather than rejecting all unfamiliar data. The ordinary MDVx wrapper does not reliably expose that parse failure as its return success: its Boolean tests whether FILE* was obtained. This is not a damage policy to copy wholesale.

positiveChecks: First length byte EOF0x100007a10..14 returns failure.
limits: 0x80 follows byte-count zero branch0x100007a50→7ab8 and returns a zero length. Do not claim this primitive rejects every invalid/indefinite BER form.
No minimal-encoding test or declared-payload/file-bound check is established by this length primitive.

positiveChecks: Each fixed field read checked; nonempty essence-label batch must have stride16 at0x10000ab34..40.
Every label read/allocation checked; error branch clears labels and frees partition0x10000ad10..20.
framingAndFailureBoundaries.compatibleExtension: Extra partition bytes produce warning0x10000ad80 then seek over declared excess; seek failure rejects pack.
limits: No global file-bound/valid essence/corruption guarantee follows from successful parsing of these pack fields.

positiveChecks: Array header read, each local tag/UID read and each entry allocation checked; errors clear/free incomplete Primer.
limits: The function receives no declared Primer value length; the recorded array itemLength is read but no stride==18 validation is visible before its count loop.

No count*stride/value-length cross-check or duplicate/conflicting mapping rejection established in this bounded function. Outer header accounting alone should not be described as universal Primer validation.

positiveChecks: 0x100045cb8 checks initial Primer key and0x100045cdc checks Primer decode.
K/L read failure, skip failure, filter failure, set-read<=0 and add-set failure propagate zero.
0x100045e8c..90 requires accumulated declared KLV count exactly HeaderByteCount at completion.
limits: Counts are advanced using declared sizes after operations. Not proof every boundary is checked before every read, every arithmetic operation is overflow-safe, or file bytes exist throughout skipped ranges.

supportedUnknown: Unknown set definition branches0x100046170..188: skip declared value; successful skip returns2 and no set. Header loop accepts positive return values.
Unregistered local tag0x1000460e4..1114 logs a warning and skips its declared local value; unknown item definition0x10004611c..128 similarly skips.
knownFailure: Known set local tag/uint16-length read, item allocation/read and failed skip all reject.
Consumed local item lengths plus four-byte framing must exactly equal known set length0x10004612c..140.
Missing InstanceUID rejects known set0x100046144→46284. Error paths free partially built item list/set.
limits: Item consumption is checked after reading/skipping, not an established before-read enclosing bound at every operation.

Known InstanceUID path0x1000460c8..d8 compares the key then loads16 bytes into set identity with no explicit item-length==16 test in that branch. This is a static validation gap, not an executed crash/exploit or universal safety finding.

framingAndFailureBoundaries.layer: Known item acquisition and typed getters
positiveChecks: mxf_read_item checks complete payload read and allocation; its length is supplied by uint16 local item framing.
UUID getter requires exactly16 bytes0x1000495a0..a8; strongref getter then requires successful dereference.
limits: Width checks do not validate all semantic values. The rational getter copies numerator/denominator without establishing a valid positive edit rate.
The separate InstanceUID direct-copy path above does not call the strict UUID getter.
UTF16 getter floors byte length/2 (0x1000499ac), with no explicit odd-byte rejection in that function. Existing Bella strict text rules must not be replaced by this behavior.

framingAndFailureBoundaries.finding: Seekable files use the backend seek callback (mxf_skip0x100007c54..7ca0); disk_file_seek0x10000866c..868c wraps fseeko and returns its status. Nonseekable fallback reads chunks and checks exact read length.
limits: A successful seek does not by itself prove skipped bytes existed. Do not describe MDVx unknown-data skipping as already proven bounded to physical file length.

structuralRequirements: Initial header partition and OP-Atom required; no new footer/run-in rescue policy established.
Singular Preface0x10000ffe0 and MaterialPackage0x100010054 required; duplicate/missing candidates rejected by mxf_find_singular_set_by_key.

optionalVersusDamaged: Genuinely absent optional field can be bypassed: PrefaceProjectName0x10000fff4→10018 and MaterialPackageName0x100010080→100a4.
When one of these optional fields exists but a called getter/conversion fails, the ami call is rejected, not independently published as a partial successful category/name result.
Other accessed optional fields can also abort otherwise useful output when present with invalid width: PackageCreationDate0x1000100c8→106e4 and ProjectEditRate0x10001003c→105e0.
cleanup: Common error path0x100010828..10864 closes wrapped file, frees header metadata/model/partition/scratch lists, then ami_free_info frees returned strings/tag arrays.
Success path0x100011ac8..11b00 frees internal file/graphs/lists but leaves returned info for caller; wrapper copies its four facts then calls ami_free_info0x10003266c.
limits: Library return code is a coarse whole-call success/error result; no explicit per-property damage/provenance object is established.
Output IDs/numeric fields can remain initialized or partly assigned on failure, while heap strings are freed; caller must not infer valid values from storage alone.

successVsFailure: Clears its old dictionary at0x10003228c..294 before opening.
Only ami result0 enters dictionary allocation0x100032410 and copies clipname/project/fileUID/matUID. Parse-error branches log then skip dictionary creation.
Final0x100032684 cmp x21,#0;0x100032688 cset w19,ne returns whether fdopen produced a FILE*, even when ami parser returned an error and closed that stream. File-open success is not parse success.
Corresponding-file caller0x1000309d8 invokes open then addInfo0x1000309e4 without testing returned Boolean; MDVxMediafile forwards according to capability flag.
nilAndDefaults: When dictionary is nil after parse failure, its objectForKey: requests yield nil; addInfo can send nil name/project to row setters.
swapUUIDfromMXFtoMDVx0x100032808 initializes a zero32-byte buffer; absent/wrong-length NSData skips swapping and still returns zero32-byte NSData at0x100032894..28a8.
On library success, a non-null string rejected by NSString UTF8 conversion is warned and replaced with empty string; a genuinely null returned string bypasses insertion.
limits: This traces attempted row setter values, not the final live UI state or proof the row becomes valid. No damaged-file runtime observed.
Do not promote zeroed/empty defaults to Bella known values or use the wrapper Boolean as a parser-success contract.

bellaImplicationsNotNewApproval: Retain explicit distinction between supported unknown data and damaged known data. Skip only when Bella has established its own containing/file bounds.
Use explicit acquisition/parse/result validity and existing agreed typed/text/identity rules; do not treat a physical file opening as metadata success or manufacture usable zero IDs.

MDVx whole-call aborts and wrapper defaults are not a reason to discard all already proven unrelated Bella fields or to adopt its exact lax checks. Root field/owner scope policy remains separately decided.
No new source priority, footer search, extra header-open rule, unsupported version recovery or arbitrary resource budget is approved by this receipt.

oldScanner.scope: Current OldScanner MXF damage boundaries by source and relevant test-source inspection. New Bella rules are recommendations only; native app and MDVx behavior covered separately.

verification.meaning: All outcomes under tests are expectations in inspected test source, not a fresh passing test run.

findings.finding: Discovery adds a physical MediaFile row and filesystem facts before any MXF parse. ScanCoordinator matches into those rows; metadata damage does not remove an already admitted physical row.

Reader validates physical extents, definite BER lengths/offset arithmetic, Partition Pack fields, HeaderByteCount boundaries, Primer batch count/stride and local property boundaries. It distinguishes Malformed, Incomplete, Unsupported, IoError and Cancelled; whole-file outcome is not the same as every field usability.

Complete bounded properties of a known type require exact fixed widths; text decoders reject odd UTF-16 units/unpaired surrogates and invalid UTF-8/ISO7. A failed interpretation marks that property Unreadable and qualifies source Incomplete while earlier/other values remain retained. Numeric semantic checks in projection can leave one rate/duration/geometry unavailable without inventing values.

Local tags acquire meaning only from that header partition's Primer. Missing/ambiguous mapping remains unmapped, not a familiar-tag guess. Duplicate Primer packs qualify Malformed and clear subsequent mappings; duplicate entries qualify Malformed and differing mappings make the tag ambiguous. Earlier properties retain their original contexts.

Root Preface/ContentStorage membership, ECD file ID, unique SourcePackage and same-partition strong-reference resolution establish ownership. Broken/ambiguous root means no file-owned projection. Broken descriptor list withholds technical dependencies; broken master/component tracks withhold master association/name/Type, while independently established file facts can survive.

Conflicting or unreadable duplicate property values fail unique() rather than selecting first. Known duplicate identity claimants remain candidates and prevent false uniqueness. Identical supported property repetitions are not automatically rejected. Equal-priority differing selected observations produce blank/unresolved value, with conflict state.

On a framing/IO failure the reader retains parsed prefix objects and still interprets them. prepareMxf projects unless cancellation is active; Projector.run checks MXF container, not Complete outcome. Coordinator qualification checks post-read existence/mtime, not source Complete outcome. Present eligible observations can therefore still supply values from an Incomplete/Malformed/IoError receipt.
findings.qualification: This is a verified static route. It does not assert an observed wrong table value or that every damaged source supplies facts. Some incomplete outcomes describe a later body truncation while the initial metadata is valid.

findings.finding: completeReferences validates captured reference properties, original ranges, target classes and matching IDs, but does not itself require completeSet(object). A structurally interrupted local-set prefix can therefore participate in ownership/reference qualification if its needed captured properties are usable. Missing unread tail could contain a conflicting occurrence, so prefix capture alone does not prove uniqueness/absence of the selected owner. A second malformed Primer also does not retroactively remove earlier property contexts.
findings.qualification: Source-level risk to avoid in fresh Bella, not a newly executed failure case. Require trustworthy complete chosen-header shared framing before publishing candidate facts; do not substitute whole-file Complete as a blanket gate.

findings.finding: Current completeSet requires every property mapped, Present, bytes retained and contiguous framing across the full set. Typed scalar/text failure can therefore suppress unrelated absence/default inferences even if the tag/length structure itself was completely traversed. This affects PCM-by-coding-absence, missing usage defaults and optional geometry defaults.
findings.qualification: Separate structural completeness from per-value usability in Bella. Then an independently bounded bad value can be isolated without permitting incomplete owner prefixes. No new runtime result was measured.

findings.finding: A safely bounded unknown mapped property, uninterpreted private value or valid external/weak reference is not automatically damaged. Unknown binary internals remain uninterpreted; unknown non-local header payloads and unsupported local-set coding are retained by range instead of loading opaque data. Generic weak references are deliberately not guessed from InstanceUID. If a field needs an unresolved/unsupported relationship it stays unavailable, while unrelated facts can remain.

Cancellation is checked during physical reads, typed decoding, graph work and acquisition; prepareMxf withholds projection when cancelled. Coordinator clears an acquisition cut short by cancellation, but retains completed qualified results for final matching without new I/O. Open failure yields IoError/Unreadable and empty projection. Reader detects changed device size as Incomplete; coordinator detected existence/mtime change excludes observations.
findings.qualification: Current checks are bounded observations, not proof against every concurrent writer or replacement preserving time/size. Size-change outcome alone is not an automatic all-facts gate in current preparation.

findings.finding: Current walks KLV framing through EOF, retains broad metadata objects/raw bytes/context/diagnostics before projection, and can perform reconciliation passes. Payloads recognized as recording/index/unknown opaque KLV are skipped/range-retained. Recognized Primer/Partition/RIP/Avid-directory values and local property bytes are still read into retained storage before some typed/count checks.
findings.qualification: This creates work/temporary storage worth simplifying but no time/RAM or crash-rate measurement is claimed. A known physical-file extent is a safety bound, not a small RAM budget. Preserve checks; avoid building unrelated graphs or buffering unneeded values in Bella.

findings.finding: One additional static wire-to-projection boundary needs verification: Boolean schema is Interpreted Uint8, ordinary interpretation delegates to numeric Uint8, while projectDropFrame accepts only QVariant Bool. The authored projection test inserts a literal true and bypasses wire decoding.
findings.qualification: This is source-path inspection, not a runtime-reproduced DropFrame failure. It illustrates why Bella should retain wire-to-final-output damage/value tests rather than only hand-authored already-decoded graphs. The previously agreed Bella DF rule remains settled.

recommendedSmallBellaBoundary.rule: Before publishing metadata from a chosen header, establish trustworthy bounded KLV/local-set extents and unambiguous required Primer meanings across the structure needed for the requested facts. Do not promote an arbitrary retained prefix after structural interruption.
recommendedSmallBellaBoundary.outsideScope: Which header copy is chosen, ordinary stop boundaries and recovery/fallback navigation are still separate pending review; whole-file Complete is not required merely because later recording/index/footer data is incomplete.

recommendedSmallBellaBoundary.rule: If the chosen header framing and owner structure are trustworthy, an unusable numeric/text value with independently known boundaries withholds only that value and calculations/labels dependent on it. Keep unrelated established facts.

A broken/ambiguous required association withholds every fact requiring that association. No guessed first package, short-ID/name match or raw-header search repairs ownership. Keep independent physical facts and separately established groups.

If the relevant structure is unsafe or ambiguous, stop using that affected header/owner metadata. Do not treat unseen remainder as absence or publish a prefix as proof that there are no competing owners/properties. Any alternate header recovery needs later navigation rules.

Defaults apply only after genuine absence is established through complete relevant structure. Unsupported mapped/private forms and valid external links are not automatically corruption. Required unsupported dependencies remain unavailable.

Keep physical rows and already completed independently qualified facts; do not publish the currently cut-short acquisition. Treat failures and observed source changes distinctly from malformed metadata. Retry/publication scheduling remains to be designed; do not invent unlimited rereads.

Retain compact selected values and needed availability/change/conflict reasons, release temporary raw header graphs/buffers. No damaged value authorizes an additional header open outside the later source/opening table.

limits: No universal corruption recovery or whole-file health claim is established.
Current retained-prefix route is not evidence that prefix data are always wrong; later essence truncation can leave complete initial metadata usable.
The static incomplete-owner/Primer and Boolean concerns are not newly observed user-file failures.
Current strict typed checks and useful tests should be carried as verified interpretation/test material, expressed through fresh small Bella helpers.
No full source priorities, extra-open rules or abnormal-header navigation are approved by this receipt.
